children: U.S. stocks rebounded from four straight sessions of losses Friday as crude oil retreated from
The relief arrived in spite of an August inflation report that pushed the market-implied odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike next week to roughly 90%.
Iranian state media said Tehran will sit down with Gulf states in Oman next week to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, and the headline was enough to knock the war premium out of crude.

West Texas Intermediate crude fell 3.0% to $99.36 a barrel, slipping back below the $100 mark it breached earlier this week. Even after Friday’s decline, WTI is up 8.6% on the week and more than 19% over the past month.
Brent crude dropped 3.0% to $104.41 a barrel, trimming a weekly gain to 8.4%. AAA reported that U.S. diesel prices hit a record high at $6.05 a gallon on Friday.
Headline consumer prices rose 0.4% month-on-month in August, the most in three months, with a 3.9% surge in gasoline accounting for over a third of the increase and the annual rate holding at 3.4%.
Core CPI rose 0.3%, above the 0.2% consensus and the fastest since April, even as the annual core rate eased to a five-year low of 2.4%.
Following the release, the probability of a hike at the Sept. 15-16 meeting jumped from roughly 70% to around 90%.
Across U.S. equity markets by midday Friday, gains were broad-based but heavily concentrated in technology.
The S&P 500 rose 1.1% to 7,674, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 566 points, or 1.1%, to 52,630.
The Nasdaq 100 rose 1.1% to 29,433. The small-cap Russell 2000 lagged, adding 0.7% to 2,910.
Gold rose 1.3% to $4,374.67 an ounce, recovering part of this week’s pullback. The CBOE Volatility Index sank 11.7% to 15.75.
